narrative: Today's batch leans heavily on connectivity and disturbance: three papers converge on how fire reshapes ecosystems, from emergency biodiversity response after Australia's Black Summer bushfires to a multi-decadal reconstruction of fire-regime transitions in the Pantanal driven by hydroclimatic disruption. Movement and corridor work is well represented, with new resistance-surface mapping identifying pinch points for tigers, leopards and elephants in southern India and range-wide connectivity priorities for jaguars across the Americas. Several papers probe trophic and mutualist reshuffling: a trait-mediated cascade shows how a single damaged-conspecific cue can suppress sea urchin grazing and protect kelp, while translocated bandicoots on Dirk Hartog Island are shown not to fully replace the fungal-dispersal roles of resident mycophagous mammals. On the applied side, restoration of drained fens in Germany and freshwater rehydration in the Everglades both track vegetation and productivity recovery over decades, and a rangeland-carnivore coexistence review cautions that reducing livestock losses to predators can inadvertently reshape grazing pressure elsewhere. Bioacoustic monitoring continues to mature quickly, with new zero-shot and contrastive-embedding approaches aimed at classifying frog and other calls across regions without extensive retraining. Together these findings point to connectivity, fire regime shift and trophic reorganisation as the week's throughlines.

methods_radar.note: Develops an integrated land-use reclassification and scenario-simulation framework distinguishing vegetation and plantation types.

methods_radar.note: Introduces an evolutionary algorithm automating frequency-band selection to shrink bioacoustic classifier models.

methods_radar.note: First application of contrastive language-audio pretraining (CLAP) to build global soundscape indices.

methods_radar.title: Colombian Caribbean mammals: A dataset of the wild mammal assemblage in the Colombian Caribbean region

methods_radar.title: Flexible use of conserved motifs constrains genome access in cell type evolution

methods_radar.title: Fourfold increase in fragmentation from road expansion in Siberian intact forests since 2000
